Class QuickMoveRoutes

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.slot.QuickMoveRoutes
public final class QuickMoveRoutes extends Object
Where a shift-click goes, on any menu, when a mod knows better than the menu. SlotKit takes over shift-click at one place for every menu (vanilla's and modded): it asks the registered routes, in registration order, for the clicked slot, and the first answer is the order the stack tries destinations in. 
// Common init (both sides: the client runs the route too, to predict the move).
QuickMoveRoutes.register((menu, player, source) -> {
    if (!sessionOpen(player)) return null;                 // no opinion
    return List.of(Dest.group(OPENED.id()), Dest.VANILLA); // the opened item first
});

How a move runs

For each destination in order, the stack merges into partial stacks, then fills empty slots, one slot at a time through vanilla's moveItemStackTo, so each slot's gate, its vetoes, SHIFT_CLICK_IN, inertness (a slot past its group's active count is skipped) and the source's own lock judge it as they judge any shift-click. The source's own group is never a destination. QuickMoveRoutes.Dest.VANILLA hands what is left to the menu's own quickMoveStack and may only come last; a route that ends without it stops there, and what doesn't fit stays put.

With no route

  • Out of a parity slot (ParityGroup), on any menu: to the player.
  • Into parity slots: groups that declared shiftClickIn(true) are tried first on the player's inventory menu, and on every other menu after the menu's own routing moved nothing (a chest takes a stack before an elytra slot does).
  • Everything else: the menu's own routing.
Whenever the menu's own quickMoveStack runs, its ranges stop short of the parity slots SlotKit appended, so vanilla never fills one by accident. Slots a menu built itself, created ones included, are its own business.

A route must answer from state both sides share (the mod's own synced session, active counts). When the two sides disagree for a tick, the server's move stands and vanilla's resync puts the client right.
